meta.competitionFrequencyPerWeek: varies — 0-3 races/week (road) or single target events / stage races; not a fixed weekly fixture
meta.notes: Low-impact, high-volume (elite riders accumulate huge weekly hours / TSS with no ground impact). The discipline drives the demand: road GC/climbing is power-to-weight + sustained aerobic; the sprint and track sprint are near-maximal neuromuscular power; the time trial is sustained threshold in an aero position. Energy-system demand varies dramatically by discipline — model it via the 'positions' (discipline) archetypes. The GYM is support: heavy strength improves cycling economy, time-to-exhaustion and sprint power (Rønnestad/Sunde/Aagaard) and protects the knee/low-back; it must never add leg fatigue that degrades a key ride or race.

maxStrength.why: Cycling is not max-strength limited, but heavy leg strength improves cycling economy and time-to-exhaustion and underpins sprint/attack force — the gym's clearest evidence-based win (more so for sprint/track).

relativeStrength.why: Power-to-weight (W/kg) is THE currency of climbing and GC performance; strength gained without non-functional mass directly raises relative power.

explosivePower.why: Sprints, attacks, accelerations out of corners and bridging moves are decided by peak neuromuscular power (decisive for sprinters/track; situational for GC).

reactiveStrength.why: Minimal stretch-shorten / plyometric demand on the bike (no ground contact); relevant only as a gym means to build RFD.

sprintSpeed.why: In-bike sprint velocity (peak power at speed) is the performance itself for sprinters; LAND sprint speed has low direct transfer, so this land quality is rated for modest relevance.

acceleration.why: Surges, attacks and corner exits in road races/criteriums; brief but often race-deciding.

deceleration.why: Minimal — descending/braking control only; no repeated land braking demand.

changeOfDirection.why: Bike handling / cornering matters, but there is no land-style multidirectional COD (higher in cyclocross/BMX, low for road).

aerobicEndurance.why: The dominant determinant of endurance cycling performance — VO2max, threshold power (FTP) and economy set the ceiling for every discipline except the pure track/sprint.

anaerobicEndurance.why: Breakaways, repeated climbs, the final kilometre and criterium efforts are heavily glycolytic — anaerobic capacity (W') and lactate tolerance decide many races.

repeatSprintAbility.why: Road races and criteriums are won on repeated surges (cover moves, corner-exits, late attacks); a single effort rarely settles a road race.

mobility.why: Hip flexion, hamstring length and thoracic mobility enable an efficient, comfortable aero position and protect the low back; not a defining performance quality but a real comfort/durability lever.
mobility.source: bike-fit & cycling low-back literature; expert consensus

stability.why: Lumbo-pelvic / core stability transfers leg power to the pedals and holds a fixed aero position under fatigue; weakness costs efficiency and drives low-back pain.

rotationalPower.why: Cycling is near-symmetric and sagittal — minimal trunk rotation demand. Low priority.

gripStrength.why: Bar control and sprint pulling on the bars use grip, but it is not a performance limiter.

neckStrength.why: Sustained cervical extension to look ahead from a flexed/aero position drives neck pain — modest relevance for durability, not performance.

balance.why: Bike handling and balance matter for safety/efficiency, but LAND balance has low transfer.

coordination.why: Pedalling efficiency, bike handling and pacing/skill are real performance contributors, though far less skill-dense than a stroke- or stick-based sport.

energySystems.workToRestRatio: discipline-dependent; road racing is a continuous aerobic base with repeated high-intensity surges, the TT is a single sustained effort, track sprint is short maximal efforts with long recovery
energySystems.matchDemands: Highly discipline-dependent: track sprint / road sprint ≈ ATP-PC / glycolytic dominant; criterium/puncheur ≈ aerobic base + repeated glycolytic surges; road race / GC climbing ≈ aerobic-dominant with decisive anaerobic moments; time trial ≈ sustained threshold (aerobic). Values above are a road-endurance-representative midpoint.
energySystems.heartRateProfile: Long stretches near aerobic/threshold with repeated spikes into VO2max+ on climbs, attacks and the finale; TT is a sustained high steady-state.
energySystems.fatigueProfile: Predominantly peripheral leg (quad) fatigue plus central fatigue over long durations; power output and the ability to repeat surges degrade late — the cycling-specific failure mode. Fuelling (carbohydrate availability) is a major co-determinant.
energySystems.source: cycling physiology (Coyle; Jeukendrup; Jones critical power); discipline-specific estimates vary — treat as indicative
energySystems.notes: Because the spectrum is so wide, the engine should read the discipline archetype (positions) rather than this single split.

primaryPatterns: repetitive pedalling (hip/knee/ankle triple extension under load)
standing/out-of-saddle climbing + sprinting (bilateral leg drive + bar pull)
movementProfile.jointLoading: High repetitive KNEE load (patellofemoral compression through flexion-extension under pedal force); sustained lumbar FLEXION load (aero/road posture); cervical extension load (head-up in a flexed trunk); perineal/saddle pressure load.
movementProfile.groundContacts: None (low-impact — the major durability advantage of cycling). Load is continuous pedal force, not impact.
movementProfile.landingDemands: None on the bike; any dryland plyometric/landing load is a deliberate added stimulus, dosed carefully.
movementProfile.jumping: None on the bike (jumps are a gym means for power/RFD only).
movementProfile.rotating: Minimal — cycling is near-symmetric and sagittal.
movementProfile.collisions: None in normal riding, but PELOTON CRASH risk is the source of cycling's severe acute injuries (clavicle, AC joint, wrist, road rash).
movementProfile.repeatedImpacts: No ground impact, but very high repetitive KNEE and lumbar cycles (the dominant cumulative overuse load).
movementProfile.asymmetricLoading: Left/right pedalling-force asymmetries, leg-length differences and cleat/saddle setup create unilateral overuse patterns to monitor.
commonDeficiencies: posterior chain (hamstring/glute) relative to quad dominance

common.name: Anterior knee pain (patellofemoral pain syndrome)
common.incidence: the most common overuse complaint in cyclists (highest of the non-traumatic injuries)
common.mechanism: high repetitive patellofemoral load through flexion-extension under pedal force; sudden volume/intensity/gear spikes; poor bike fit (low saddle, fore-aft, cleat malalignment); quad dominance / weak hip abductors
common.rtpConsiderations: Address bike fit FIRST, then graded volume, hip + quad strengthening, cadence/gearing management.
common.source: Clarsen 2010 (overuse injuries in pro road cyclists); Wanich 2007 (lower-extremity cycling injuries)

common.name: Low back pain (flexion / sustained-posture)
common.incidence: very high (the most reported overuse pain alongside the knee)
common.mechanism: prolonged lumbar flexion + static loading in the riding/aero position; weak lumbo-pelvic endurance; limited hip/hamstring/thoracic mobility; bike fit too long/low
common.rtpConsiderations: Core endurance (McGill-style anti-flexion/anti-extension), hip mobility, bike-fit review, progressive aero-position tolerance.
common.source: Clarsen 2010; cycling low-back literature; expert consensus

common.name: Neck / cervical pain
common.mechanism: sustained cervical extension to look ahead from a flexed trunk; static load on cervical extensors; aggressive aero position
common.rtpConsiderations: Neck isometrics, thoracic mobility, position/fit adjustment, gradual aero exposure.

common.name: Iliotibial band syndrome / lateral knee pain
common.mechanism: repetitive friction at the lateral knee from cleat malalignment, leg-length asymmetry, sudden volume spikes; weak hip abductors
common.rtpConsiderations: Cleat/fit correction, hip-abductor strengthening, load management.

common.name: Pressure / compression neuropathies (saddle + handlebar)
common.mechanism: sustained perineal pressure (pudendal — numbness/saddle sores) and ulnar/median pressure at the bars (handlebar palsy, carpal compression) from prolonged static loading
highRiskTissues: ulnar / median nerve at the wrist

modifiable: core support reducing weight on hands

common.rtpConsiderations: Bike-fit / saddle review, hand-position variation, core support; usually conservative.
common.source: cycling overuse / neuropathy literature; expert consensus

common.name: Crash trauma (clavicle fracture / AC joint / wrist / road rash)
common.incidence: the signature ACUTE cycling injury (peloton/descending crashes)
common.mechanism: high-speed falls; outstretched-hand or shoulder impact; the clavicle is the classic cycling fracture
common.rtpConsiderations: Medically managed (often surgical fixation for clavicle); graded return; maintain aerobic fitness on a trainer where safe; rebuild bone-loading + upper-body capacity.

injuryProfile.summary: Two faces: a long tail of OVERUSE injuries (the upside of a no-impact sport) — anterior knee pain and low-back pain lead, with neck, ITB and saddle/bar neuropathies behind — almost all modifiable via BIKE FIT, strength and load management; and ACUTE crash trauma (clavicle fracture the signature), which strength can only partly mitigate. Cycling is also non-osteogenic, so bone health is a background concern the gym should serve.

positions.name: GC / Climber (road)
positions.role: General-classification + climbing — power-to-weight over sustained climbs and stage races.
positions.movementDemands: Sustained high aerobic output; repeated VO2max efforts on climbs; long durations.
positions.runningDemands: n/a (in-bike); decisive sustained + repeated climbing power.
positions.strengthReq: moderate (relative-strength / economy focus, minimal added mass)
gymPriorities: low-volume heavy strength for economy (no mass)
positions.recoveryConsiderations: Highest aerobic volume — keep gym low-fatigue so it never blunts climbing legs.

positions.name: Sprinter (road)
positions.role: Bunch-sprint finisher — peak neuromuscular power off a long aerobic day.
positions.movementDemands: Repeated positioning surges then a maximal 10-20 s sprint; lead-out craft.
positions.bodyComposition: Powerful, muscular, higher mass than climbers.
gymPriorities: heavy strength + power (squat, hip thrust, jumps, Olympic-lift derivatives)
positions.recoveryConsiderations: Tolerates and benefits from more gym power work; place it away from sprint-quality days.

positions.name: Time-trialist (TT)
positions.role: Race against the clock — sustained threshold power in an aero position.
positions.movementDemands: Single maximal sustained effort at/near threshold; static aero posture.
positions.recoveryConsiderations: Position tolerance is trainable — core/mobility carry as much value as raw strength here.

positions.name: Criterium / Puncheur
positions.role: Short, sharp races + punchy finishes — repeated maximal surges.
positions.movementDemands: Continuous corner-exit accelerations and repeated short maximal efforts on an aerobic base.
positions.recoveryConsiderations: High glycolytic + crash exposure — manage freshness and handling fatigue.

positions.name: Track sprinter
positions.role: Pure short-duration maximal power (match sprint, keirin, 200 m, kilo).
positions.movementDemands: Maximal neuromuscular power; standing starts; very short efforts with full recovery.
positions.strengthReq: very high (the gym-heaviest cyclists — heavy squat / Olympic lifts core to the event)
positions.bodyComposition: Highly muscular, high lean mass — the most powerful cyclists.
commonInjuries: low back pain (heavy lifting + standing starts)
gymPriorities: maximal strength + power (heavy squat, hip thrust, Olympic lifts, jumps)
positions.recoveryConsiderations: Strength training IS event preparation here — periodise it like a strength/power athlete.

positions.name: Endurance / Gran Fondo / Domestique
positions.role: Sustained durability over very long durations; support roles.
positions.movementDemands: Very long aerobic output; fatigue-resistance and fuelling over hours.
positions.recoveryConsiderations: Highest volume exposure — durability + recovery, gym strictly low-fatigue.

assessments.name: Functional threshold power (FTP) test
assessments.purpose: Sustainable threshold power (20-min or ramp-derived) — the core training-zone anchor and a key performance benchmark; report absolute W and W/kg.

targets.elite: high W/kg; improving at fixed body mass

assessments.source: cycling training-zone practice (Allen & Coggan); expert consensus

assessments.name: VO2max / maximal aerobic power (ramp test)
assessments.purpose: Aerobic ceiling (VO2max / MAP) — sets the upper bound on endurance performance and informs VO2max-interval prescription.

assessments.name: Peak power profile / sprint power (5-15 s) + Wingate
assessments.purpose: Neuromuscular peak power (sprint) and anaerobic capacity (W') — discipline-defining for sprinters/track and decisive moments for road.

targets.elite: high peak W + W/kg; discipline-relevant W'

assessments.name: Maximal lower-body strength (squat / trap-bar 1RM or 3-5RM)
assessments.purpose: Dryland max strength — the evidence-based lever for cycling economy, time-to-exhaustion and sprint power; track relative to body mass.

targets.elite: strong relative to mass; maintained in-season

assessments.name: Countermovement jump (CMJ)
assessments.purpose: Lower-body power proxy + daily neuromuscular-fatigue monitoring (a drop flags accumulated fatigue).

targets.elite: track trend; within ~10% of baseline for freshness

assessments.name: Bike-fit + hip/hamstring/thoracic mobility screen
assessments.purpose: Position-related injury screen — hip flexion, hamstring length, thoracic extension/rotation and saddle/cleat setup drive knee/low-back/neck overuse.

assessments.name: Core / lumbo-pelvic endurance battery
assessments.purpose: Trunk-endurance baseline (e.g. plank / side-plank / Sorensen holds) — supports position tolerance and low-back protection.

youth.trainingEmphasis: Skill, aerobic enjoyment, bodyweight + band strength, mobility; build bone-loading habits (cycling is non-osteogenic). Avoid early specialisation and overload.
commonMistakes: skipping bike fit during growth spurts

lowest: in-season fatigue from novel gym work
development.trainingEmphasis: Build FTP/VO2max, lay a real strength base for economy, embed core + bike-fit habits, introduce TSS/volume monitoring.

lowest: non-specific hypertrophy that adds non-functional mass
senior.trainingEmphasis: Individualise to the discipline; maintain strength/power at low fatigue; protect the knee/back; nail event tapers.
commonMistakes: dropping strength in-season (losing the economy gain)

elite.trainingEmphasis: Data-led individualisation; precise strength + taper periodisation; protect availability around a dense race calendar.

masters.trainingEmphasis: Maintain strength/power (counter age-related loss + cycling's non-osteogenic nature), manage volume conservatively, protect joints, longer recovery.

offSeason.primaryObjective: Build aerobic base + a genuine gym strength foundation; restore knee/back health and mobility.
offSeason.trainingEmphasis: High aerobic volume (zone 2), heavy gym strength (the best phase to build it — improves economy), core, mobility, bike-fit review.

programming.source: cycling S&C (Rønnestad & Sunde 2010): off-season rounds out (upper + bone-loading the sport lacks); in-season is leg-economy-specific

preSeason.primaryObjective: Convert base to discipline-specific power/threshold; build race-pace capacity; shift gym from strength to power.
preSeason.trainingEmphasis: Threshold + VO2max + race-pace intervals, gym power (lower volume, explosive intent), maintain core; reduce gym volume as bike intensity rises.

programming.source: cycling S&C (Rønnestad & Sunde 2010): off-season rounds out (upper + bone-loading the sport lacks); in-season is leg-economy-specific

competition.primaryObjective: Maintain qualities; sharpen; keep strength with minimal fatigue; peak for target events.
competition.trainingEmphasis: Race-specific intensity, MAINTAINED strength at low volume (1-2 short heavy sessions — preserves the economy gain), full core/prehab, freshness management.

programming.source: cycling S&C (Rønnestad & Sunde 2010): off-season rounds out (upper + bone-loading the sport lacks); in-season is leg-economy-specific

playoffs.primaryObjective: Peak taper for a target event or stage race.
playoffs.trainingEmphasis: Reduced volume, maintained intensity, sharpening; gym is priming/maintenance only; maximise recovery and fuelling.
testingRecommendations: readiness monitoring only — no fatiguing tests

recovery.primaryObjective: Physical and mental recovery; restore knee/back; address carried niggles.
recovery.trainingEmphasis: Low/unstructured riding, mobility, light cross-training + bone-loading; rehab any carried knee/back issues.
testingRecommendations: none; medical review of carried knee/back issues

oneMatchPerWeek.pattern: Built around key quality rides (threshold/VO2max/race); gym placed to NOT fatigue the legs before quality or racing.
oneMatchPerWeek.heavyDay: early-week, away from key quality rides and racing (often paired with an easier ride)
oneMatchPerWeek.injuryPreventionDay: core + knee/hip prehab embedded; primary strength dose early-week
oneMatchPerWeek.typicalLoadingPattern: Strength + base early → threshold/VO2max mid → sharpen → easy pre-race → race.
avoidHeavyLiftingDays: day before a key quality ride

twoMatchesPerWeek.pattern: Two races / hard rides in a week: recovery-first between them; no heavy gym.
twoMatchesPerWeek.heavyDay: none (or a very light maintenance dose mid-block)
twoMatchesPerWeek.powerDay: CNS priming only on race mornings if used
twoMatchesPerWeek.recoveryDay: between the two efforts + after each
twoMatchesPerWeek.typicalLoadingPattern: Race → recovery → race → recovery. Gym is priming/maintenance only.
avoidHeavyLiftingDays: both race days + the day before each

tournamentOrCongested.pattern: Stage race / dense block (consecutive race days): pure freshness + fuelling management.
tournamentOrCongested.typicalLoadingPattern: Protect recovery + fuelling between stages; gym is priming, never development.

transfersWell: back / front squat (max strength → economy + sprint power)
trap-bar deadlift + Romanian deadlift (posterior chain, balance quad dominance)
Bulgarian split squat + single-leg work (correct L/R asymmetry)
leg press (high-load quad strength, low skill — in-season maintenance)
core anti-flexion + anti-extension + anti-rotation (position tolerance, force transfer)
limitedValue: high-volume bodybuilding hypertrophy that adds non-functional mass (hurts W/kg, especially for climbers)
heavy bilateral rotational/COD work (no transfer to a sagittal sport)
endless high-rep core flexion (crunches) — endurance/anti-movement core transfers more
long slow grinding gym circuits that just add leg fatigue
accessoryPriorities: posterior chain (hamstring/glute) to balance quad dominance
hip abductors / glute medius (knee tracking, ITB)
gymPhilosophy.singleLegEmphasis: Moderate-high — pedalling is alternating single-leg; split squats, single-leg RDLs and step-ups correct left/right force asymmetries and protect the knee, while bilateral squats build the heavy strength.
gymPhilosophy.olympicLiftingSuitability: Optional/advanced — high value for TRACK/sprint power if competent; for road riders, jumps + hip thrust deliver much of the power benefit at lower technical/fatigue cost.
gymPhilosophy.plyometricEmphasis: Moderate, dosed — cycling is non-impact, so dryland jumps/throws add a deliberate impact + RFD + bone-loading stimulus; progress off a strength base.
gymPhilosophy.coreTrainingPhilosophy: Endurance + anti-movement dominate: anti-flexion / anti-extension to hold the riding position, and anti-rotation to transfer leg power to the pedals without energy leak. Minimal high-volume flexion.
gymPhilosophy.neckTraining: Low-moderate priority — light neck isometrics + thoracic mobility address the sustained-extension neck pain of long/aero positions.
gymPhilosophy.rotationalTraining: Low — cycling is symmetric and sagittal; train anti-rotation (Pallof) rather than rotational power.
gymPhilosophy.isometricTraining: Useful — core/position holds, tendon-friendly low-fatigue strength in-season and for knee/tendon rehab.
gymPhilosophy.tempoRecommendations: Controlled tempo for prehab/core; explosive concentric intent for strength + power (intent drives RFD); avoid grinding fatigue near key rides.
gymPhilosophy.velocityRecommendations: Heavy strength at high intent + low reps for economy/power; the legs are the limiter, so prioritise quality and recovery over gym volume in-season.

exercises.name: Leg press
exercises.secondaryAdaptation: in-season strength maintenance with low spinal load

exercises.name: Calf raise (straight + bent knee)
exercises.primaryAdaptation: lower-leg strength + ankle stiffness (pedal force transfer)

injuryPreventionLibrary.recommendedFrequency: strength 2x/week + bike-fit review; mobility most days
exercisesToAvoid: heavy deep-knee load during a flare
monitoringRecommendations: bike-fit at season start + on any niggle
low-back soreness check on long-ride weeks
injuryPreventionLibrary.source: Clarsen 2010; McGill core-endurance literature; expert consensus

warningSigns: neck/upper-back ache on long or TT rides

decisionRules.if: athlete reports anterior knee pain/soreness OR knee niggle after volume/gear increase
decisionRules.then: review bike fit (saddle height/fore-aft, cleat) FIRST; reduce volume + heavy deep-knee loading; emphasise hip-abductor/glute + pain-free strength; flag for review

decisionRules.if: athlete reports low-back pain linked to riding/aero position
decisionRules.then: emphasise core endurance + hip/thoracic mobility; review bike fit (reach/drop); reduce heavy spinal-loaded lifting and abrupt aero-ride-duration increases
remove high-soreness gym (heavy strength, novel plyometrics, high-volume eccentric); allow only low-fatigue priming

decisionRules.if: a key quality ride or race is scheduled within 24 hours
decisionRules.then: avoid heavy/high-volume lower-body gym the day before (preserve leg freshness for the bike)
gym is CNS priming only (a few jumps/sprints) or none; no strength development
cap this week's volume; do not add lower-body gym volume; monitor knee/back daily
decisionRules.source: Gabbett 2016 (contested — Impellizzeri 2020 / Lolli 2019); applied to cycling TSS

decisionRules.if: readiness score low (poor sleep + high soreness + low wellness)
decisionRules.then: autoregulate down one step; prioritise easy aerobic / recovery; do not test
treat as neuromuscular fatigue: reduce gym-power + high-intensity bike load, emphasise recovery, recheck

decisionRules.if: athlete reports systemic illness (fever / below-neck symptoms)
decisionRules.then: withhold training until symptom-free; resume gradually

decisionRules.if: in taper phase before a target event
decisionRules.then: reduce TOTAL volume substantially (~40-60%) over ~1-3 weeks while MAINTAINING intensity; keep low-volume gym priming; maximise recovery + fuelling
MAINTAIN strength at minimal effective volume (1-2 short heavy sessions/week, low volume, away from key rides) — do not drop it, or the economy/power gain regresses
prioritise heavy lower-body strength alongside aerobic base — this is the phase that improves cycling economy and time-to-exhaustion

acwr.model: acute (7-day) : chronic (28-day) of training load (TSS) and/or ride volume/duration; rolling/EWMA preferred
acwr.source: Gabbett 2016 applied to cycling TSS — methodology contested (Impellizzeri 2020, Lolli 2019); soft monitoring input

loadManagement.weeklyProgressionGuideline: Avoid >~10-15% week-to-week spikes in ride volume / TSS; the knee and low back are the load-limited tissues for overuse.

gymVolumeRanges.inSeason: low maintenance (1-2 short heavy sessions; low volume, high quality) + core/prehab

loadManagement.minimumEffectiveVolume: ~1-2 short heavy gym sessions/week SUSTAIN the strength/economy gain in-season (Rønnestad); core/knee prehab should not drop below a low weekly dose.
loadManagement.maximumAdaptiveVolume: Off-season — build gym strength + aerobic base here, when fatigue tolerance is highest.
loadManagement.maximumRecoverableVolume: Constrained by total ride volume + leg-fatigue tolerance; gym must never compromise key ride quality — total LEG load is the binding ceiling.
loadManagement.deloadRecommendations: Planned deload every 3-5 weeks in build phases; auto-deload on knee/back-soreness flags, CMJ drop, or load ACWR >1.5. The event taper is a planned, performance-oriented deload.
loadManagement.progressionRules: Progress gym load when quality is met at target RPE and the knee/back are symptom-free; prefer intensity over volume in-season.
loadManagement.regressionRules: On knee/back flags or red readiness, drop gym volume first; never schedule heavy lower-body gym the day before a key ride or race.
loadManagement.missedSessionRules: Do not stack missed gym sessions; resume at planned level. After time off (esp. crash/knee), rebuild ride volume + gym load gradually.
loadManagement.source: Mujika/Bosquet (taper); Rønnestad (strength + maintenance); Gabbett (load — contested); expert consensus

thresholds.when: high quad/knee soreness or a knee niggle
thresholds.modifier: cut heavy lower-body gym + high-intensity bike efforts; easy aerobic + prehab only; check bike fit
convert to recovery / easy aerobic ride

factors.name: Previous session RPE / TSS (bike + gym load)

thresholds.modifier: treat as accumulating fatigue; ease load

thresholds.when: stage race / multiple races in a block

readinessModel.notes: Leg/quad soreness is elevated to a top-weight, cycling-specific readiness input (the knee is the overuse target). Subjective wellness + sleep + prior load (sRPE/TSS) carry the most general weight; objective vitals (HRV/RHR) are trend signals. Raw vitals stay private to the athlete; a coach sees only the derived readiness score (see TEAM-ARCHITECTURE.md).

coachDashboard.principle: Coach sees DERIVED and availability signals only — never an individual's raw HRV/sleep/resting-HR. Aggregated, plain-English, action-oriented.
mostUsefulKpis: training availability (fit/modified/out — esp. knee/back + crash recovery)
weeklyReports: training load vs plan (squad + per discipline group)
coachDashboard.trafficLightIndicators: Per-rider green/amber/red from the derived readiness + load state (no underlying numbers shown).
coachDashboard.privacyNote: All per-athlete entries here are DERIVED (readiness score, load_state, ACWR, adherence %, injury availability). Raw vitals are excluded by design and enforced by the schema validator.

in-season strength MAINTENANCE preserves the gains (Rønnestad 2010)
the taper improves performance — reduce volume, maintain intensity (Mujika/Padilla; Bosquet 2007)

weakEvidence: exact ACWR thresholds applied to cycling TSS (contested)
bike-fit interventions reducing injury INCIDENCE (mechanistically strong, RCT evidence modest)
CMJ as a precise sprint-performance predictor in cyclists
Olympic-lifting superiority over jumps/hip-thrust for road power

kpis.measurementMethod: FTP (W) divided by body mass (kg) — the climbing/GC currency; also report absolute W

kpis.name: Knee / low-back availability

athleteDashboardKpis.name: Sprint power

athleteDashboardKpis.name: Mobility / position score

athleteDashboardKpis.name: Recovery score
athleteDashboardKpis.why: Teaches that recovery (and the taper) is training; nudges sleep/soreness habits.

athleteDashboardKpis.name: Availability streak
athleteDashboardKpis.why: Celebrates knee/back-healthy, on-the-bike time — the ultimate goal, framed positively.

coachDashboardKpis.name: Squad readiness
coachDashboardKpis.why: At-a-glance freshness (traffic-light, derived) to shape the session before it starts.

coachDashboardKpis.name: Training availability
coachDashboardKpis.why: Who is fit / modified / out (esp. knee/back + crash recovery) — the key planning input.

coachDashboardKpis.name: High-risk athlete flags

coachDashboardKpis.name: Recovery trend (squad)

performanceScore.philosophy: Reflects progress toward the demands of competitive cycling, weighted to discipline-relevant qualities, rewarding consistency and (knee/back) availability and penalising excessive fatigue/poor recovery — never rewarding training through knee/back pain or red readiness.

components.rationale: Consistency drives adaptation across a high-volume programme.
Knee/back-healthy, crash-free availability is the strongest performance lever.
FTP / W·kg is the core road-performance outcome.
Sprint/peak power is a controllable, decisive margin (discipline-weighted).
Gym strength underpins economy + sprint power (evidence-based gain).
Position range/comfort is both performance and protection.
Penalises chronic fatigue/poor recovery; keeps the score sustainable.

guardrails: never increases for training through knee/back pain, red readiness or injury
consistency + availability dominate so the score can't be gamed by occasional max efforts
fatigue/recovery caps the score when recovery is poor
does not reward added mass that worsens W/kg
performanceScore.explainability: Each component is shown with its contribution so the rider sees why the score moved and what to work on next.

gamification.name: Knee/back-healthy weeks
gamification.rewards: Consecutive weeks available + completing knee/back prehab — motivation tied to the sport's key overuse injuries.

gamification.name: Consistency streak
gamification.rewards: Unbroken weeks hitting prescribed rides + gym sessions; rewards process over outcome.

gamification.name: Strength/prehab badge
gamification.rewards: Completing the strength + core/prehab programme each week — makes the unglamorous (but economy-boosting) work visible.

gamification.name: Position / mobility milestone
gamification.rewards: Reaching/maintaining hip + thoracic ROM targets for a comfortable aero position.

gamification.name: Testing-battery completion
gamification.rewards: Completing each testing block (FTP / power profile / squat / CMJ) — encourages objective tracking.

gamification.name: Personal-best milestones
gamification.rewards: FTP, W/kg + gym PRs vs the rider's own baseline — self-referenced, not leaderboard.

gamification.name: Long-term development arc
gamification.rewards: Season-over-season power + capability growth — frames the long game over short-term volume grinding.
